intent: Added two sensors to the existing 5-sensor array to create a 7-sensor symmetric layout, improving lateral line coverage and reducing line loss events. Maintained sensor size at 0.016 m and wheel track at 0.16 m for stability and coverage. Mass kept at 0.7 kg for acceleration. Expect fewer line loss events, lower rms error, and improved completion rates, especially on the challenging slalom track where no finishes occurred previously.
rationale: The previous iteration increased sensor size to 0.016 m, widened the wheel track to 0.16 m, and reduced mass to 0.7 kg, aiming to reduce line loss events and steering oscillation while improving acceleration and progress. However, the race data shows persistent line loss events (0.35-0.4) and no finishes on the slalom track, indicating coverage and stability issues remain. Steering oscillation is still moderate to high (0.37-0.45), and control effort has increased, suggesting the controller is working harder to maintain line tracking. To address this, I propose adding two additional sensors to the array (increasing from 5 to 7) to improve line coverage and reduce line loss events, especially in complex track sections. I will keep the sensor size at 0.016 m to maintain good coverage and noise tolerance. The wheel track remains at 0.16 m to preserve stability benefits. Mass remains at 0.7 kg to retain acceleration advantages. Sensor positions will be symmetrically spaced across the front, extending coverage laterally to better detect line edges and reduce loss. Wheel radius, body width, and body length remain unchanged to isolate sensor geometry effects. I expect this denser sensor array to reduce line loss events and rms error, improve line detection in sharp curves, and help the integrator achieve smoother steering and better progress, especially on the slalom track where no finishes occurred previously.
